headings.title: Notebook discovery, reads and output previews

html:
Notebook discovery, reads and output previews

Task Context finds retained material through scope-local references, then asks its owning store for an authorized public representation. The lexical index narrows a search; it does not establish ownership, copy every source body or add inference. The context and memory guide owns notebook policy and read settings. Saved assistant context describes explicit message selection and its additional preparation/dispatch checks.

Publishing discovery metadata

flowchart TD Owner[Run checkpoint or source-owner transaction] --> Document[Stable reference, locator and source value] Document --> Digest[Hash stable JSON and compare locator metadata] Digest -->|Exact unchanged document| Skip[Keep existing signature and postings] Digest -->|Changed or reintroduced| Signature[Publish signature and locator] Signature --> RAM[RAM document-change hook] Signature --> SQL[Explicit SQL posting update] RAM --> Membership[Unique parent, term and accepted-input memberships] SQL --> Membership Owner --> Projection[Selected historical field projections] Owner --> Attachment[Attachment and owned setup locators] Artifact[Registered artifact owner] --> Lifecycle{Artifact state} Lifecycle -->|Available| Document Lifecycle -->|Deleted| Withdraw[Withdraw postings and retain deletion marker] Membership --> Browse[Bounded discovery] Projection --> Read[Owner-checked source reads] Attachment --> Read Browse --> Read

index.py hashes a stable JSON representation of the source value and compares the current index version, withdrawal state and all locator metadata. An exact match avoids a write. A metadata change with the same source digest reuses the previous terms. The document stores terms and a locator; signatures live in document membership records. A missing parent section is registered in the same transaction.

lexical.py maintains one membership per reference/bucket. All documents have an immediate-parent bucket. Non-section documents have Unicode case-folded term memberships. User messages and accepted user requests also enter the accepted-input bucket. Parent-filtered term queries include the exact reference and its slash-delimited descendants, so a prefix sibling such as facts/a- is outside facts/a.

The resident store updates ordered roots through its document-change hook; SQL updates its membership rows explicitly. Only RAM maintains the global membership diagnostic count. Posting changes occur within the source owner's transaction. They neither grant access nor attest that a stored assertion is true.

Checkpoint integration creates stable sections and references. Current field projections update only for the notebook's active epoch. Selected historical state and accepted parameter fields are retained as schema-tagged source projections, avoiding whole historical run-snapshot loads for those reads. Attachment locators retain grant scope; setup projections are registered only by their source run. Artifact discovery requires an owning notebook run and indexes metadata, not file bytes. Deletion withdraws postings and leaves a deletion marker so recovery does not rediscover a deliberately withdrawn source.

Listing, search and continuation

sequenceDiagram participant Caller as Task Context caller participant Browse as browse.py participant Index as Scope-local postings participant Service as Source/access service participant Views as Bounded read views Caller->>Browse: List parent or search words, optional cursor Browse->>Service: Validate parent and authenticate scoped cursor alt New query Browse->>Index: Select buckets and capture their last keys else Continuing a saved window Browse->>Views: Load query/epoch-bound reference manifest Views-->>Browse: Candidates, signatures and next keyset position end opt Need a new candidate window Browse->>Index: Read after previous key through captured upper key Index-->>Browse: At most 128 ordinary posting candidates end loop Until result count or serialized-entry budget is reached Browse->>Service: Recheck reference access and current signature alt Source changed or is unavailable Browse->>Browse: Record bounded gap metadata else Search candidate Browse->>Service: Resolve current public source Service-->>Browse: Authorized and redacted body Browse->>Browse: Recheck terms and form short excerpt else List candidate Browse->>Browse: Return source metadata end end opt Newly built window remains unfinished Browse->>Views: Retain reference/signature manifest after read view closes end Browse-->>Caller: Entries, gaps, coverage, completion and next cursor

browse.py lists immediate children or searches within a reference subtree. List defaults to 10 entries and allows 1–50; search defaults to five and allows 1–20. Search requires at least one word and accepts all or any. all starts from the smallest term posting; any uses term buckets and assigns a match to its first matching query term to avoid duplicate results. work/recent uses the notebook head's recent references instead of ordinary posting windows.

An ordinary candidate window holds at most 128 references plus source signatures. The continuation records an exclusive last-seen key and a captured inclusive upper key per bucket. Deleting an earlier row does not shift that position. This is not a frozen snapshot of every future page: a later insertion inside the remaining key range may appear when a new window is built. Retained candidates are checked against their captured signatures; changed or unavailable ones become gaps.

Search reads the current public body and checks terms again after redaction before returning an excerpt of up to 240 characters, starting near the first matching term. Kind filters and hidden matches may leave a page sparse or empty. That does not alone mean the search is complete. Serialized entries are limited to 4,000 characters; gap reporting has a separate approximate 900-character threshold and an omitted marker. These are response budgets, not model-token counts.

The service authenticates cursors with the notebook key and scope. Browse identity also binds query, parent, matching mode, kinds, epoch and representation version. The notebook keeps only its eight most recent read-view manifests, which contain references and signatures rather than source bodies. Evicted, malformed, cross-scope, changed-query or old representation cursors must restart. The response's notebook coverage metadata and its pagination completion answer different questions.

Resolving and paging a source

sequenceDiagram participant Caller as Task Context caller participant Service as TaskContextService participant Owner as Books / requests / source owner participant Store as Journal, projection, receipt or file store participant Page as Read page builder Caller->>Service: Read reference, optional pointer/cursor and character limit Service->>Owner: Resolve special reference or scope-local entry alt Reference is a section Service-->>Caller: section_requires_list and concrete list action else Readable source Owner->>Owner: Check ownership, sequence/grants and source-specific access Owner->>Store: Load retained source representation Store-->>Owner: Source value or unavailable failure Owner->>Owner: Apply origin policy and current redaction Owner-->>Service: Public source value Service->>Page: Resolve JSON Pointer and source-bound cursor alt Invalid pointer or changed source identity Page-->>Caller: Explicit pointer or stale-cursor failure else Valid page Page->>Page: Clamp to captured limits and applicable attachment policy Page-->>Caller: Unicode text, source metadata, completion and continuation end end

The resolver uses the owning representation: journal messages, retained receipts, notes/books, accepted requests, selected checkpoint fields, verified attachments or registered artifacts. Live ownership, source sequence and branch grants constrain access where applicable; source-specific stores retain their own checks. Stored projections and search postings cannot substitute for them. Source policy and current secrets/redaction apply before content is returned.

read treats resume/current, current fields, accepted requests and Books sources through their dedicated resolvers. Reading a section returns a concrete list action. For ordinary pages, a JSON Pointer selects the value before serialization. An absent operation stdout/stderr/output field reports available pointers instead of inventing a stream from combined output. Invalid pointers provide a bounded root-read action.

Page identity includes the reference, pointer and current serialized public text. A changed representation invalidates its old cursor. Limits count Unicode characters and are clamped by the task's captured maximum and, for attachments, applicable attachment read policy. The envelope reports the effective limit, clamping, source size, offset, originating run and completion. Follow returned continuations; a partial page is not a complete observation.

Operation previews and recovery

flowchart TD Receipt[Retained operation receipt and origin policy] --> Restricted{Content restricted?} Restricted -->|Yes| Metadata[Lifecycle metadata without stream bodies] Restricted -->|No| Cache[Cache protected tails of available streams] Cache --> Error[Include distinct envelope error when present] Error --> Render[Reserve recovery hints and divide remaining stream space] Render --> Explicit[Explicit preview with field continuations] Render --> Automatic[Automatic progress projection] Automatic --> Log{Backing-log action available?} Log -->|Yes| Job[Prefer concrete manage_job logs action] Log -->|No| Fields[Use receipt-field recovery actions] Job --> Facts[Preserve coverage, range and unavailable-source facts] Fields --> Facts Facts --> Model[Allowlisted operation metadata and incomplete markers] Metadata --> Model Explicit --> Caller[Caller chooses whether more evidence is needed] Model --> Caller

output_preview.py caches up to 320 characters from the end of each available stdout, stderr, output and error field, including an omission marker within that allowance. The shared tail helper avoids retaining an unrecognizable secret suffix across the clipping boundary. A distinct envelope error can be included when no corresponding data error exists. Restricted content exposes neither stream text nor capture fields.

Rendering reserves controller-generated field/capture hints, limits command text and divides the remaining space across individual tails, preserving shorter streams first. It does not truncate the assembled preview from the end and thereby lose an error tail. Required recovery wording can exceed a very small requested budget; outer preparation accounts for preview-budget overhead. This is not a guarantee that every complete envelope fits an arbitrarily small character limit.

Receipt continuations identify actual fields and obey the captured read limit. Automatic progress prefers a backing job-log action when incomplete receipt output has a usable job reference; otherwise it retains receipt-field actions. Purged logs, evicted earlier ranges and capture failure remain distinct unavailable-source facts. A recovery action cannot recover output that was never retained, and displaying one does not execute it.

Automatic operation entries use an explicit metadata allowlist, omit routine default flags, retain active job/activity identities and mark truncated material incomplete. Non-operation entries retain their authored content/provenance. Explicit reads keep their normal envelopes and policies. Preview success, command exit status and full source observation are separate facts.

Index recovery and diagnostic failures

flowchart TD Recovery[Recover resident records or upgrade SQL index] --> Cache[Discard obsolete disposable cache structure] Cache --> Keep[Retain document locators, signatures and withdrawal markers] Keep --> Owner{Live, compatible notebook owner?} Owner -->|Deleted or tombstoned| Skip[Skip discovery without deleting source records] Owner -->|Missing or incompatible| Quarantine[Retain one ownership-quarantine record] Owner -->|Proven| Withdrawn{Source withdrawn?} Withdrawn -->|Yes| Skip Withdrawn -->|No| Rebuild[Recreate valid memberships] Rebuild --> Ready[Bounded browsing available] Failure[Task Context adapter failure] --> Catalog{Namespaced error registered?} Catalog -->|Yes| Named[TaskContextError catalog lookup] Catalog -->|No| Legacy[Legacy kind lookup] Named --> Diagnostic[Stable diagnostic identity and recovery guidance] Legacy --> Diagnostic

Resident recovery filters out old heads/pages and non-document membership rows, then rebuilds disposable roots. SQL migration runs once for index version three, preserving signatures and withdrawal markers while clearing obsolete cache rows. Ownership verification skips deleted history and tombstoned sources without deleting them; absent or incompatible owners are quarantined once per reference. rebuild itself adds valid memberships rather than clearing every existing root. Only the source/deletion owners may remove retained evidence.

diagnostics.py resolves a known TaskContextError:<kind> or falls back to the legacy kind. It passes available expected/current revisions to the shared error catalog and returns stable identity and next-step guidance. Classification does not retry the operation or change notebook state.

Verification and limits

Focused checks in controller optimization cover index churn, recovery roots, keyset deletion and old-cursor rejection. Task Context hardening covers focused discovery without historical snapshot loads, changed-source gaps, origin redaction and partial-output observation. Tail-preview tests exercise tail/error preservation, small budgets, concrete recovery calls and cache upgrade behavior across supported store fixtures. The RAM case skips the SQL-only cache migration. These are isolated fixtures; they do not certify every storage failure mode or launch model, Gateway or user workloads.
